node.title: F1 case (iii): intermediate-subfield tower recursion
node.statement: Case (iii) closes: intermediate-subfield-confined slopes are priced by the same two mechanisms one level up, recursively, with per-level denominators printed. NOTE: critical only if the official family admits non-generating rows (Q0.1). | TOWER DEPTH DATUM (2026-07-07, M_B audit, notes/correspondence/MB_VS_F1_LEDGER.md section 5 + nodes/f1_case_tower/notes/mb_tower_depth.md): at KoalaBear-shaped official rows (n = 2^21, q = p^6) the recursion's practical depth is governed by the v13.2-corrected census (the earlier 'practically depth-one' reading is RETRACTED as numerically empty per v13_2_discrete_subfield_census_guard + notes/correspondence/MB_VS_F1_LEDGER.md; forced correction #333) — the intermediate-level floors M_{p^d}(d1), d = 2,3,6, are dead by ~2.09M/4.18M/10.45M bits at the deployed profiles; only the base level carries mass. Per-level denominators q_K = p^d confirmed as the correct normalization (they reproduce upstream's PROVED M_B floors at d = 1 and their refuted q-scale models at d = 6). || V13.2 CENSUS CORRECTION (2026-07-20, wave-15, w15-C3; the 2026-07-07 TOWER DEPTH DATUM preserved): Paper D v13.2 repairs the soft-mean normalization at levels p^2,p^3,p^6 — the earlier 'depth one in practice' inference was numerically empty and is REFUTED (node v13_2_discrete_subfield_census_guard + the corrected correspondence ledger notes/correspondence/MB_VS_F1_LEDGER.md); this node's PROVED tower-depth content is unaffected as a function of the corrected census.
node.notes: PROVED (maintainer assembly): minimal-field descent kills the tower case at the bottom; two proved ledgers per level; admissibility by axis8.
